headline: High-risk orchestration pair: Kestra can write and egress broadly while Rasa can relay messages, creating default-path leakage and action-cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can read/write files and emit messages/notifications, while Rasa ingests chat text over Slack/Messenger/Twilio. If Kestra-generated content is routed into Rasa channels, prompt-like instructions can be injected through shared text surfaces. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertain.
conditions: IF Kestra outputs are forwarded into a Rasa channel without sanitization
IF Rasa treats inbound message text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Add a strict content filter between Kestra outputs and Rasa inputs
Prefix all machine-generated messages with non-executable markers
Disable any auto-action parsing on Rasa inbound text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and can egress broadly; Rasa handles text/voice and can send messages through chat APIs. If shared data is routed from Kestra into Rasa, sensitive workflow content can leak into external messaging surfaces. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows contain sensitive inputs, logs, or artifacts
IF Rasa forwards those contents to external messaging providers
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff to Rasa
Restrict Rasa channels to non-sensitive test data
Turn off message echoing and transcript forwarding
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra supports multiple instances and writes to filesystem paths, while Rasa does not support multiple instances and has only allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a shared mutable resource or overlapping write scope, so direct conflict is limited and likely requires unusual orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same workspace or shared files
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking
mitigations: Separate filesystem paths per agent
Run only one writer per shared directory
Add file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: introduce a coordination layer for mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra can generate workflow outputs, logs, and notifications; Rasa is a dialogue agent that can consume text and emit responses over chat channels. If Rasa treats Kestra output as authoritative, a bad workflow result can cascade into incorrect user-facing replies or actions. Verification is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Kestra output is passed into Rasa without a verification step
IF Rasa uses that output to answer users or trigger downstream messages
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step before Rasa consumes Kestra output
Require structured schemas for all Kestra-to-Rasa handoffs
Mark workflow results as untrusted in the chat layer
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches database and cloud-storage data and can send notifications through third-party services; Rasa handles conversational text/voice and can relay messages via external channels. If regulated data is present, differing retention and residency obligations can be violated by the handoff. The profiles do not specify certifications, so the compliance risk is inferred and uncertain.
conditions: IF regulated data is included in Kestra workflows
IF that data is forwarded through Rasa channels with different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Block regulated data from chat channels
Set short retention on transcripts and workflow logs
Document a shared data-handling policy
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
